notFound.title: Page not found
notFound.text: This page does not exist, or your roles do not give access to it.

organisations.title: Organisations
organisations.subtitle: One organisation per customer, each with its owner, members and products.
organisations.empty: No organisation yet. Create the first one with the "New organisation" button.

create.title: New organisation
create.name: Name
create.nameDescription: Lowercase letters, digits and hyphens. Cannot be changed later: it is the identifier.
create.nameInvalid: Lowercase letters, digits and inner hyphens only
create.emailDomainsDescription: Users with these domains are sent to this organisation when they log in. Press Enter or a comma after each domain.
create.ownerDescription: First and last name are required with an email. An existing user is reused (with their own names), but some cannot be added to this organisation: a member of another organisation, or an administrator of the realm.

teams.hint: Managed by the org admins: what each team gives its members. Open a team to see its members, products and roles.

delete.title: Delete the organisation {{org}}?
delete.message: Its client, its groups and the products assigned to it are deleted. The users are kept, but lose their access to the organisation. This cannot be undone.

disable.title: Disable the organisation {{org}}?
disable.message: Its members are disabled too: they can no longer log in, and their sessions are closed (a token already issued stays valid until it expires, 5 minutes by default). No member can be added while it is disabled. Enabling it again enables the same members.

enable.title: Enable the organisation {{org}}?
enable.message: The members disabled with the organisation can log in again. A member disabled for another reason stays disabled.

products.subtitle: What the organisation negotiated for each product: the features it bought, its quotas, its parameters. The API of the product counts the usage.
products.removeMessage: The members of the organisation lose this product.

assign.title: Assign a product to {{org}}
assign.noProductLeft: Every product of the catalogs is already assigned
assign.boughtFeaturesDescription: The features of the product the organisation bought: its teams can give these, never more.
assign.boughtFeaturesRequired: Choose at least one feature: a metered product gives nothing else
assign.meteredHint: A product with metered features has no quota of its own: the organisation gets a quota for each metered feature it buys.
assign.tokenHint: In the tokens, once a team of the organisation gives the product:

catalogs.title: Catalogs
catalogs.subtitle: Your APIs, grouped as you sell them. Each catalog comes out as one claim in the tokens.
catalogs.empty: No catalog yet. Create the first one with the "New catalog" button.

catalogForm.name: Name
catalogForm.nameDescription: Lowercase letters, digits and hyphens. Cannot be changed later: it is the name of the claim and of the scope the applications ask for.
catalogForm.nameInvalid: Lowercase letters, digits and inner hyphens only

delete.title: Delete the catalog {{catalog}}?
delete.message: Its client and its scope are deleted: the applications that ask for it no longer get it in their tokens. This cannot be undone.
delete.notEmpty_one: The catalog still has {{count}} product: delete it first, the catalog can only be deleted once empty.
delete.notEmpty_other: The catalog still has {{count}} products: delete them first, the catalog can only be deleted once empty.

products.title: Products
products.subtitle: Each product is an access to one of your APIs, with the features an organisation can buy and the parameters it negotiates.
products.empty: No product yet in this catalog.

token.title: What your APIs receive in the tokens
token.scope: An application gets this catalog by default, or asks for it with
token.kinds: Here billing is a simple product (an access role, one quota), shop a product with metered features (no access role, one quota per metered feature, in a claim of its own).
token.usage: Orgkeep does not count the usage: your API compares its own counters with the limits of the token.

introspection.title: Introspection credentials for your APIs
introspection.description: With lightweight tokens (see the login client), your APIs read the content of the tokens by introspection (RFC 7662), authenticated with these credentials. It also works with full tokens: an API can switch before the tokens do.
introspection.audience: These credentials only introspect the tokens of this catalog: a token without it, or of a user with no right in it, is answered "active": false.
introspection.shownOnce: Copy the secret now: it is not shown again. Generating another one replaces it.

confirm.title: Generate a new secret for {{catalog}}?
confirm.message: The previous secret stops working at once: every API of this catalog must get the new one.

roles.title: Roles
roles.subtitle: Valid for the whole catalog, not for one product: what a user may do in this environment (searcher, beta-tester...). Your API combines them with the products of the user.

catalogRoleForm.name: Name
catalogRoleForm.nameDescription: Lowercase letters, digits and hyphens. Cannot be changed later: it is the name in the tokens.
catalogRoleForm.nameInvalid: Lowercase letters, digits and inner hyphens only
catalogRoleForm.orgGrantableDescription: On: the org admins give it to their teams. Off: reserved, only you give it, to a user (test accounts, partners...).
catalogRoleForm.orgGrantableWarning: Turning this off removes the role from the teams of every organisation. Users who got it from you keep it.

catalogRole.grantableHint: The org admins give it to their teams, in the organisations with a product of this catalog. You can also give it to a user below.
catalogRole.reservedHint: Reserved: only you give it, to a user below.

delete.title: Delete the role {{role}}?
delete.message: It is removed from the teams and from the users who have it. This cannot be undone.

users.title: Given by you
users.subtitle: Users who hold the role directly, whatever their teams. Only members of an organisation.
users.removeMessage: {{user}} loses the role (unless a team gives it).

token.title: In the tokens
token.scope: Only when the token has the catalog: by default, or asked with

productForm.name: Name
productForm.nameDescription: Lowercase letters, digits and hyphens. Cannot be changed later: it is the role name in the tokens.
productForm.nameInvalid: Lowercase letters, digits and inner hyphens only

features.description: The permissions an organisation buys and its teams give (e.g. read, write), or the capacities it buys with a quota each (metered, e.g. an engine). They can also be added later.
features.name: Feature name
features.meteredHint: A metered feature is bought with its own quota. One metered feature is enough: the product then has no quota of its own, only a quota per metered feature. Cannot be changed later.

params.description: What each organisation negotiates besides its quota and cycle, which every product has (e.g. a region).
params.name: Name
params.valuesDescription: Press Enter or a comma after each value.
params.valuesRequired: A list needs at least one value

delete.title: Delete {{product}}?
delete.message: Its features and its parameters are deleted with it. This cannot be undone.
delete.assigned_one: The product is assigned to {{count}} organisation: remove it from the organisation first.
delete.assigned_other: The product is assigned to {{count}} organisations: remove it from these organisations first.

kind.simpleHint: One quota per organisation for the whole product, and an access role in the tokens.
kind.meteredHint: No quota of product nor access role: one quota per metered feature an organisation buys. This stays so while the product is assigned to organisations.

features.title: Features
features.subtitle: An organisation buys some of them, and its teams give them to their members. A metered feature is bought with its own quota.
features.nameDescription: Lowercase letters, digits and hyphens. In the tokens: {{product}}:<name>
features.meteredFixed: Chosen when the feature was created: delete it and add it again to change it.
features.empty: No feature: the product is a plain access.
features.removeMessage: The organisations that bought it lose it, and their members no longer get it in their tokens.

params.title: Parameters
params.subtitle: Negotiated by each organisation besides its quota. Changed with the "Edit" button above.
params.empty: No parameter besides the quota and its cycle.

token.title: In the tokens
token.hint: For a member of an organisation that bought every feature, with an example quota. The parameters show their defaults.
token.meteredHint: For a member of an organisation that bought every feature, with example quotas: no access role, a claim per metered feature with its quotas. The pool "/" is the one of the organisation: your API keys its counters by organisation, catalog, product, feature and pool.

tokenPreview.title: Token of {{member}}
tokenPreview.catalogsDescription: Those an application asks for: by default, every catalog where the organisation has a product.
tokenPreview.hint: The claims of the access token your APIs receive for this member, computed by Keycloak without the member logging in. Only the claims: nothing here can be used to call an API.
tokenPreview.lightweight: The login client issues lightweight tokens: the token carries nothing but who the user is, your APIs read the rest by introspection.
tokenPreview.notInAudience: Not in the audience of the token: {{catalogs}}. The APIs of these catalogs get "active": false when they introspect it (the member has no right in them).

members.title: Members of {{org}}
members.loadError: Could not load the members of {{org}}

disable.title: Disable {{member}}?
disable.message: The member can no longer log in and their sessions are closed. A token already issued stays valid until it expires. The member stays in the organisation, their teams and products.

enable.title: Enable {{member}}?
enable.message: The member can log in again.

members.removeMessage: The member leaves the organisation {{org}} and its teams, and loses their products. The account is kept.

form.title: Add a member to {{org}}
form.invitation: A new user receives an email to choose a password. The member joins the team users.

teams.title: Teams of {{org}}
teams.subtitle: A team gives products of the organisation and catalog roles to its members. The team users holds every member: what it gives, everybody has.
teams.loadError: Could not load the teams of {{org}}
teams.deleteMessage: Its members lose what it gives, unless another team gives it too.

form.title: New team in {{org}}
form.name: Name
form.nameDescription: Lowercase letters, digits and inner hyphens. It cannot be changed afterwards.
form.nameInvalid: Lowercase letters, digits and inner hyphens only
form.poolHint: With a quota of team, its pool is named "{{pool}}" in the tokens.

team.hint: What this team gives reaches the tokens of its members at their next login or token refresh.
team.usersHint: Every member of the organisation is in this team: what it gives, everybody has.
team.realmOwnerHint: You manage this team as an org admin of {{org}} would: its org admins see the same changes.

members.title: Members ({{count}})
members.removeMessage: The member loses what this team gives, unless another team gives it too.

products.title: Products ({{count}})
products.noneAssigned: The organisation has no product yet: the realm owner assigns them.
products.orgPoolPerFeature: pools of the org, per feature
products.removeMessage: The members lose this product, unless another team gives it.

catalogRoles.title: Catalog roles ({{count}})
catalogRoles.hint: Valid for every product of the catalog: what the APIs combine with the products of the user.
catalogRoles.empty: The team gives no catalog role.

grant.title: Give a product to {{team}}
grant.productPlaceholder: Choose a product of the organisation
grant.featuresDescription: Among those the organisation bought. None: the product alone.
grant.featuresDescriptionMetered: Among those the organisation bought. At least one: the product gives nothing else.
grant.meteredHint: The members share the quota of the organisation for each metered feature (pool "{{pool}}" in the tokens). No quota of team for the product itself: a feature can have its own.
grant.featureQuotas: Quotas of team, per metered feature
grant.featureQuotasDescription: Optional: a budget shared by the members, on top of the pool of the organisation for the feature. Pool "{{pool}}" in the tokens. A member in several teams with a quota for the feature gets all their pools.
grant.quotaDescription: Optional: a budget shared by the members, on top of the pool of the organisation ({{quota}} / {{cycle}}).
grant.quotaInvalid: A whole number greater than 0, or empty
grant.poolHint: Pool "{{pool}}" in the tokens. A member in several teams with a quota for the product gets all their pools.

loginClient.title: Login client
loginClient.subtitle: The client the users of every organisation log in through, to your applications.
loginClient.loadError: Could not load the login client

details.title: For your developers
details.flow: A public client: your applications use the authorization code flow with PKCE, no secret.
details.console: Anything else (themes, identity providers, sessions) is in the Keycloak console of your realm, with your own account:

settings.title: Your applications
settings.noRedirectUri: No redirect URI yet: nobody can log in through this client.
settings.redirectUrisDescription: Where users come back after login. https (http on localhost only); a wildcard only at the end: https://app.example.com/*. Press Enter after each URI.
settings.postLogoutRedirectUrisDescription: Where users come back after logout. Same rules.
settings.webOriginsDescription: Origins allowed to call Keycloak from a browser (CORS): https://app.example.com, or + for the origins of the redirect URIs.
settings.defaultCatalogsDescription: In every token of this client. The other catalogs are only in a token when the application asks for them (scope=<catalog>).

orgkeepApi.title: Your own admin screens (Orgkeep API)
orgkeepApi.description: To build your own screens on the API of Orgkeep instead of this dashboard, they log in with this client: same login page, no catalog in its tokens, never lightweight. Set the URIs of those screens here, with the same rules.
orgkeepApi.loadError: Could not load the client of the Orgkeep API

lightweight.title: Lightweight tokens
lightweight.description: When the tokens get too big (many products and features), the tokens of this client can carry only who the user is: no roles, no catalogs, no profile, always the same small size. Your APIs then read the content by introspection, a standard call (RFC 7662) that Spring, Quarkus and the gateways know.
lightweight.introspection: Each API introspects with the credentials of its catalog, generated on the page of the catalog:
lightweight.marker: Each lightweight token carries the claim

confirm.title: Turn on the lightweight tokens?
confirm.message: Every application of this client receives lightweight tokens at once. Each of your APIs must introspect the tokens first (it works with full tokens too), or it no longer sees the rights of the users. An application that reads roles in the access token in the browser no longer sees them either; the ID token does not change.
